history.period: Ramakrishna Mission work in Arunachal Pradesh since 1966; Itanagar branch centre of Belur Math
history.summary: FLAG: IDENTITY AMBIGUOUS. No standalone public 'Ramakrishna Mission Temple' could be verified on the web for Itanagar. The Ramakrishna Mission's Itanagar branch centre (listed among Belur Math's Arunachal Pradesh centres) is the Ramakrishna Mission Hospital campus near Ganga Market / the Itanagar helipad (P.O. R.K. Mission, Itanagar 791113) - a working hospital, not a standalone temple. The Mission began work in then-NEFA in 1966 at the request of local leaders and the state administration and on the personal appeal of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, starting with education; the Itanagar hospital followed at the urging of then Lt. Governor K.A.A. Raja and local leadership. Most RKM branch centres include a shrine/prayer hall, but no source found describes a separate temple building open to the public at this centre - this should be verified on the ground. Recommend the record be treated as the hospital-campus shrine (or removed) rather than as an independent temple.

name: Ramakrishna Mission Temple
town_description: Itanagar, the capital of Arunachal Pradesh in the Papum Pare district, sits in the Himalayan foothills and is named after the historic Ita Fort ('fort of bricks'). Key attractions include the Ita Fort, the Jawaharlal Nehru State Museum, Ganga Lake (Gekar Sinyi), Indira Gandhi Park and the hilltop Buddhist Gompa.

travel.airport: Lilabari Airport (Assam) is the commonly cited nearest airport in travel guides; the newer Donyi Polo Airport (Holongi) now serves the Itanagar region (verify distance).
travel.railway: Naharlagun Railway Station, approx. 12-15 km from Itanagar.
travel.road: Ramakrishna Mission Hospital campus near Ganga Market / Itanagar Helipad, P.O. R.K. Mission, Itanagar 791113; autos and taxis run from Itanagar town.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March, when the weather is pleasant.
visitor_information.opening_hours: No published visiting hours for any shrine on the campus; the hospital is a working medical facility (verify before visiting).
